news.headline: Seahawks rule out LT Charles Cross and WR Rashid Shaheed
news.detail: Seattle's final report (Nov 1) has left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), receiver Rashid Shaheed (knee) and running back Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring) out. Josh Jones moves to left tackle, and he left the Kansas City game with a hamstring problem. Linebacker Uchenna Nwosu is listed as doubtful, per Bleacher Nation's roundup.

news.headline: Sam Darnold has no injury tag and starts for Seattle
news.detail: Darnold has no designation on the final report (Nov 2). Backup Drew Lock (elbow) is questionable. Seattle also traded for guard Quenton Nelson last week.

news.headline: Bears QB Caleb Williams healthy; RB Monangai out again
news.detail: Williams is back after a three-game hamstring absence and has thrown for 613 yards in two wins. RB Kyle Monangai is out for a fourth straight game, so D'Andre Swift leads the backfield. Corner Malik Muhammad and linebacker D'Marco Jackson are questionable. TE Colston Loveland has no designation. TE Cole Kmet is out for the year (Nov 2 reports).

news.headline: Calm, dry weather forecast for Lumen Field
news.detail: Forecasts for the 8:15 PM ET kickoff call for about 50 degrees, wind of 1 to 2 mph and almost no chance of rain. Weather should not push the total either way.

news.headline: Jaxon Smith-Njigba has no injury designation for Chicago
news.detail: He appears only as a rest-day (not injury) entry on Seattle's practice reports and is not among the players ruled out. He led the NFL with 867 receiving yards entering the game, and had 150 yards on 9 catches last week against Kansas City.

He has had 5 or more catches in all five games on his ESPN log, but two of those were exactly 5, so there's little room for error.

He reached 9 catches in 3 of those 5 games (10, 12, 9). Chicago's defense has given up under 70 rushing yards per game, which could push Seattle to the air.

NFL.recap: Week 8 went well for the model. It picked 11 of 12 winners (Arizona over Dallas was the miss) and went 9-4 against the spread. The over/under was even at 6-6. Many of the misses were efficiency or finishing-drive swings, such as Jacksonville 42, Indianapolis 7 and Pittsburgh 27, Cleveland 6, which the model can't see before kickoff. The season spread record is still below .500 at 18-21-1, and its average miss (9.8) is a little worse than Vegas's (9.1).

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different winner than the Vegas favorite, it has mostly lost so far.
lessons.evidence: 2 of 7 graded games where the model's side was not the Vegas favorite won (CIN over BAL and DEN over KC won; PHI over DAL, NYG over NO, ATL over CHI, PHI over CAR, NE over CHI lost). LV-NYJ had the model even, so it isn't counted.
lessons.test: On past seasons, take every game where the model's pick differs from the moneyline favorite. Compare its win rate and spread record with Vegas. Wait for 20+ games.

lessons.lesson: Large gaps between the model's total and Vegas's total have not paid off.
lessons.evidence: 0 of 5 graded games with a gap of 4.9 or more won the over/under pick (NE-CHI at 5.0 and PHI-WAS at 6.2 are the latest). Smaller gaps are mixed: DAL-ARI at 4.2 lost, BAL-BUF at 3.9 won. Overall the over/under is 20-19.
lessons.test: On past seasons, group games by size of the total gap (under 2, 2-4, over 4). Check hit rate per group. Needs 20+ games in the large-gap group.

lessons.lesson: Many big misses come from efficiency swings, which the model can't see before kickoff.
lessons.evidence: In 8 of the 14 games where the winner was wrong, the review names efficiency as the main reason (DAL-PHI, TB-CAR, NYG-HOU, ARI-LA, CHI-ATL, CAR-PHI, BAL-CLE, ARI-DAL). Turnovers led in NO-NYG and SF-ATL. MIA-NYJ and NE-CHI were close. HOU-JAX had no clear reason.
lessons.test: On past seasons, measure how often big spread misses (over 8 points) are driven by efficiency versus turnovers. Check whether the model's misses are larger than Vegas's overall.

lessons.lesson: Big-game player picks are close to the model's chances on hit rate, but still lose units.
lessons.evidence: 8 of 25 big-game picks hit, against 8.3 expected, at -7.46 units. The earlier shortfall (5 of 18 against 5.9) has mostly closed. Milestone picks are 20 of 26 against 19.5 expected.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual hit rate for long-shot props in buckets of model chance. Also check whether the prices paid are shorter than fair odds. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

lessons.lesson: Best-value picks against the sportsbook are running below the model's chances.
lessons.evidence: 7 of 16 best-value picks hit this season, against 8.5 expected, at -2.64 units. Several sit only 0.4 to 1.5 points over break-even.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check hit rate of the model's top value picks by size of edge. Needs 20+ picks.

lessons.lesson: The model's margin errors are larger than Vegas's, and it is below .500 against the spread.
lessons.evidence: Average spread miss is 9.8 for the model against 9.1 for Vegas over 39 graded games. The model is 18-21-1 against the spread (9-4 in week 8). Winners are 25 of 39.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare the model's average absolute margin error with Vegas's, by week, over a full season. Also check ATS record by season. Do this before changing anything.

lessons.lesson: Big gaps between the model and Vegas may come from lineup changes the model hasn't picked up.
lessons.evidence: DAL at PHI listed Hurts, who was on IR, and DAL won 38-21 against the model's PHI by 3.9. PHI at WAS listed him again, the model had WAS by 3.3 against Vegas -6, and WAS won 27-10: the model's side won, but the spread was lost. Possible case: TB-CAR. Far under 20 games.
lessons.test: On past seasons, flag games where a starting QB differed from the one in the model's inputs. Compare the model's margin error in those games with all others. Needs 20+ such games.

lessons.lesson: Most-likely-winner picks have fallen short of the model's own chances.
lessons.evidence: 9 of 16 most-likely-winner picks hit this season, against 11.8 expected, at -4.51 units. Overall winners are 25 of 39 (64%).
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (70-79%, 80%+) and compare hit rate with the moneyline-implied chance. Needs 20+ picks per bucket.

news.headline: Georgia State QB Cameran Brown ruled out; Ayden Pereira to start
news.detail: The Sun Belt availability report on Oct 31 rules out Georgia State's starter Cameran Brown. Ayden Pereira, who threw two touchdowns and two interceptions last week, starts against Coastal Carolina.

news.headline: Kansas QB Isaiah Marshall is a game-time call at TCU
news.detail: Marshall was cut from probable to questionable on Oct 29-30 and is reportedly a game-time decision. Cole Ballard would start if he can't go. Kansas is also missing running back Jalen Dupree and two defensive backs, and TCU is without leading rusher Payne.

news.headline: Iowa State keeps Raynor at QB; backup Moberly out
news.detail: Coach Rogers confirmed Jaylen Raynor starts. Backup Connor Moberly is listed out on Thursday's report. Iowa State's offense has struggled, with four injured receivers done for the season, while Oklahoma State averages 40 points a game. Oklahoma State tight end Carson Kolb is out and safety Quinton Hammonds is questionable.

news.headline: Indiana QB Josh Hoover probable with a throwing-arm injury
news.detail: Hoover played hurt against Michigan, going 8 of 18 for 81 yards. He is probable for Minnesota. Minnesota will be without tight end Pierce Walsh and center Ashton Beers. Indiana is only 1-6 against the spread this year.

news.headline: Missouri RB Ahmad Hardy returns; Arkansas WR Chris Marshall questionable
news.detail: Hardy makes his season debut after recovering from an offseason gunshot wound, per CBS Sports on Oct 30. Arkansas's top receiver Chris Marshall is questionable with a leg injury and has been out since the Vanderbilt game.

news.headline: Southern Miss QB Ethan Hampton may return from broken hand
news.detail: Hampton is probable after missing about five games with a fractured throwing hand. A pregame report still expects Landry Lyddy to start, so who plays is unclear.

Georgia State's starting QB is out, which helps Coastal Carolina; but the model's own margin of Georgia State by 13.7 doesn't fit a 51% cover chance for Coastal, so read this pick with care.
The model has East Carolina by 12.0 against a line of 4, which doesn't match a 50.9% cover chance for Temple; no injury news changed this.

College.recap: Week 9 games so far went poorly for the model. It picked 4 of 9 winners, went 2-7 against the spread, and was 5-4 on overs and unders. Four favorites lost outright (Kent State, UCF, James Madison, Western Kentucky), and both games where the model liked its favorite 3+ points more than Vegas failed to cover. The Top picks lists are at 10 of 12 on likely winners, 6 of 15 on value picks (7.6 expected, -3.55 units) and 5 of 15 on underdogs (5.5 expected, +0.99 units).

lessons.lesson: The 'model total 3+ above Vegas means the over hits' pattern does not hold up; if anything the over hit less often.
lessons.evidence: Week 8: over hit in 8 of 17 such games. Week 9 so far: 1 of 5 (only Baylor-UCF went over). Combined that is 9 of 22 (41%). I treat the earlier Week 7-8 count of 8 of 13 as overlapping, so I'm not adding it.
lessons.test: On past seasons, group games by model total minus Vegas total (0-3, 3-6, 6+) and check how often the over hits in each group. Need 20+ games per group.

lessons.lesson: Big misses mostly show up as efficiency gaps; turnovers and finishing drives come second.
lessons.evidence: Week 8 results: of 25 games missed by 8+ points, efficiency was named first in 15, turnovers in 4, finishing drives in 4, and nothing stood out in 2. Earlier sets showed the same (17 of 24; 12 of 17). Week 9 results had no reviews. Efficiency is measured after the game, so it partly restates the miss.
lessons.test: On past seasons, check whether a team's success rate in prior games predicts the model's error next game. Also compare turnover margin and points per trip inside the 40 with the long-run average, to see if misses lean one way or are random.

lessons.lesson: When the model picks a different favorite than Vegas, results are mixed.
lessons.evidence: About 4 of 9 right overall as of last run. None of the 9 Week 9 games listed had the model on a different side than Vegas, so there is no new data. Sample is tiny.
lessons.test: On past seasons, list games where the model and Vegas disagree on the winner, then compare the model's win rate with Vegas's. Need 20+ games.

lessons.lesson: The earlier lean that the favorite fails to cover when the model likes it 3+ points more than Vegas is not settled.
lessons.evidence: Week 8: favorite covered in 7 of 14 such games. Earlier: 2 of 9. Week 9 so far: 0 of 2 (Tulane, Western Kentucky lost the cover). Overlap between sets can't be confirmed, so I won't total them.
lessons.test: On past seasons, take games where the model's favorite margin is 3+ points above Vegas's and check the cover rate by size of gap (3-6, 6+). Need 20+ games per group.

lessons.lesson: The 'Best value against the sportsbook' list has been weak so far.
lessons.evidence: Season: 6 of 15 hit against 7.6 expected, at -3.55 units. The edges are thin (about 51% against 52.4% needed). Fewer than 20 picks. Also, the Coastal Carolina and Temple picks sit oddly against the model's own large margins for the favorites.
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's spread and total picks by edge size and compare hit rates with the 52.4% break-even. Check that each pick's cover chance matches the model's own margin. Need 20+ games per bucket.

lessons.lesson: Underdog picks are close to what the model expected, and slightly ahead on units.
lessons.evidence: Season: 5 of 15 hit against 5.5 expected, at +0.99 units. The early edge came and went. Under 20 picks.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare predicted chance with actual win rate for the model's underdog picks, in buckets of model chance (under 35%, 35-45%). Needs 20+ picks.

lessons.lesson: The 'Most likely winners' list has landed close to the model's own chances.
lessons.evidence: Season: 10 of 12 hit against 10.5 expected, at -0.61 units. The prices are very short, so one miss costs a lot. Only 12 picks.
lessons.test: On past seasons, bucket the model's top win chances (90%+, 85-90%) and compare with actual win rate and with Vegas's no-vig chance. Need 20+ games per bucket.

lessons.lesson: The model's spread misses are larger than Vegas's over the season.
lessons.evidence: Season (125 games): average spread miss 12.1 points for the model against 11.2 for Vegas. The gap was 0.9 last run too. Winners right in 80 of 125 (64%) and a 56-64-3 spread record. Week 9 so far: 4 of 9 winners right, 2-7 against the spread.
lessons.test: On past seasons, compare the model's and Vegas's average spread error. Then test whether averaging the model's margin and Vegas's margin beats either alone, and whether the gap changes by week of season.
